name: OWASP API Security Top 10
source_notes: Names and descriptions from the official owasp.org API Top 10 2023 page; prevention condensed from the official OWASP/API-Security repo, editions/2023/en.
caveats: No post-2023 edition or draft was found; 2023 is treated as current.
Only the release year (2023) is verified; no exact date in the notes.
Maturity "production" comes from the OWASP projects data for the API Security Project (level 3.5); the numeric-to-label mapping is inferred.
The notes attribute no CWEs to API Top 10 items, so cwe arrays are empty.
detection entries are reinhardt heuristics, not OWASP text; "(inferred) " related links are reinhardt mappings.

items.name: Broken Object Level Authorization
items.summary: APIs expose endpoints that take object identifiers; without an ownership check in every function that loads data by a client-supplied ID, users can access other users' objects.
prevention: Base authorization on user policies and hierarchy.
In every function that uses client input to access a record, check the caller may act on that record.
Prefer random, unpredictable IDs (GUIDs) as defense in depth.
Write tests that verify the authorization mechanism.

static: Handlers reading req.params.id / params.id / body.userId and querying (findById, .eq("id", id), doc(db, "x", id), prisma findUnique) with no owner predicate
Supabase tables without RLS or policies using (true)
Firebase rules with if true or auth != null without resource.data.uid == request.auth.uid
Server clients built with service_role/secret keys querying by user-supplied ID

items.name: Broken Authentication
items.summary: Authentication mechanisms are implemented incorrectly, letting attackers compromise tokens or assume other users' identities.
prevention: Know every authentication flow; OAuth and API keys are not user authentication.
Do not reinvent token generation or password storage.
Treat password recovery like login, with rate limiting and lockout.
Require re-authentication for sensitive changes and offer MFA.
Apply anti-brute-force controls stricter than general rate limits and reject weak passwords.

static: jwt.decode used instead of jwt.verify; unpinned algorithms or none allowed
Hard-coded JWT secrets (secret, changeme)
Login/reset routes without rate limiter
API keys used as user authentication
Tokens stored in localStorage (debatable)

items.name: Broken Object Property Level Authorization
items.summary: Combines 2019's Excessive Data Exposure and Mass Assignment: APIs return or accept object properties the caller should not read or change.
prevention: Avoid generic serializers like to_json()/to_string(); return only chosen properties.
Avoid auto-binding client input into objects.
Allow updates only to properties the client may change.
Validate responses against a schema and return minimal data.

static: res.json(user) / NextResponse.json(row) returning full DB rows including password hash, role or isAdmin
Model.create(req.body), update(req.body), Object.assign(entity, req.body), Supabase .update({...body})
select("*") results sent to clients
review: Which fields each role may see or modify

items.name: Unrestricted Resource Consumption
items.summary: Requests consume CPU, memory, bandwidth or paid third-party services (email, SMS, phone, biometrics) without limits, causing denial of service or higher costs.
prevention: Limit memory, CPU, restarts and file descriptors.
Cap payload, string, array and upload sizes.
Rate limit per endpoint and throttle sensitive operations such as OTP checks and password recovery.
Validate page-size/limit parameters server-side.
Configure spending limits or billing alerts for all provider integrations.

static: No express-rate-limit / rate-limiter-flexible / Upstash ratelimit in deps or middleware
express.json() without limit; multer without limits
Unbounded limit/take query params
LLM/SMS/email calls (OpenAI, Twilio, Resend) in unauthenticated routes

items.name: Broken Function Level Authorization
items.summary: Unclear separation between administrative and regular functions lets users call functions they should not have access to.
prevention: Deny by default and grant explicit access per role.
Have admin controllers inherit from a base controller that checks role.
Check role inside admin functions placed in regular controllers.

static: Admin routes (/admin, /api/admin/*, deleteUser) with no role check
Role checks only in client route guards
isAdmin read from request body or headers

items.name: Unrestricted Access to Sensitive Business Flows
items.summary: A business flow (e.g. buying tickets, posting comments) is exposed without considering how automated abuse could harm the business; not necessarily an implementation bug.
prevention: Identify business flows that could be harmed by excessive use.
Use device fingerprinting and human detection such as captcha or biometrics.
Detect non-human usage patterns.
Consider blocking Tor exit nodes and known proxies, and secure machine-facing APIs.

static: Signup, checkout, comment or invite routes with no captcha (Turnstile/hCaptcha/reCAPTCHA) or throttle (heuristic)

items.name: Server Side Request Forgery
items.summary: The API fetches a remote resource from a user-supplied URI without validating it, letting attackers make the server send requests to unintended destinations.
prevention: Isolate the resource-fetching mechanism in the network.
Allowlist remote origins, URL schemes, ports and media types.
Disable HTTP redirection following.
Use a well-maintained URL parser and validate input.
Do not send raw responses back to clients.

static: fetch(req.body.url), axios.get(userUrl), got(params.url) with no allowlist
Image proxy or link-preview endpoints
Next.js images.remotePatterns with hostname "**"
review: Network segmentation and metadata endpoint exposure

items.name: Security Misconfiguration
items.summary: APIs and supporting systems are misconfigured, for example missing hardening, permissive cloud permissions, missing TLS, permissive CORS or verbose errors.
prevention: Use a repeatable hardening process and review orchestration files and cloud permissions.
Use TLS everywhere, including internal traffic.
Disable unused HTTP verbs and restrict content types.
Implement a proper CORS policy and security headers for browser clients.
Enforce response schemas, including errors, to avoid leaking stack traces.

static: cors({ origin: "*", credentials: true }) or reflected origin
No helmet
Error handlers returning err.stack
NODE_ENV not production or debug flags
Public S3/GCS buckets in IaC; open Firebase Storage rules

items.name: Improper Inventory Management
items.summary: Poor inventory of hosts and API versions leaves deprecated versions and debug endpoints exposed.
prevention: Inventory all API hosts with environment, network exposure and version.
Document integrated services, auth, errors, redirects, rate limiting, CORS and endpoints, generating docs in CI.
Restrict API documentation to authorized users.
Protect all exposed API versions and do not use production data in non-production.

static: Both /api/v1 and /v2 present
/debug, /test, /api/seed or /api/reset routes
Swagger UI exposed without auth
.env.example containing production URLs
review: Which hosts and versions are actually deployed

items.name: Unsafe Consumption of APIs
items.summary: Developers trust data from third-party APIs more than user input and apply weaker security standards to it.
prevention: Assess the security posture of API providers.
Use TLS for all integrations.
Validate and sanitize data received from integrated APIs.
Allowlist redirect locations and do not blindly follow redirects.

static: Webhook handlers without signature verification (e.g. Stripe constructEvent missing)
LLM output used in SQL, HTML or shell
redirect: "follow" to third-party URLs
